newsitem.title: USA: Brooke Group says settles class action suit.
newsitem.headline: Brooke Group says settles class action suit.

text.p: Brooke Group Ltd. said Thursday that it and its Liggett Group tobacco subsidiary had reached a settlement in a federal class action suit in West Virginia that essentially stopped all class action and individual tobacco lawsuits against Liggett nationwide.
In return, Brooke and Liggett, the smallest of the cigarette makers, agreed to cooperate in prosecuting conspiracy claims against other tobacco companies, Brooke said in a statement.
In March, Liggett agreed to settle the 22 Medicaid suits from states seeking to recover the health care costs of smokers that had been filed at that time.
Under the pact, Liggett, which is owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group, agreed to turn over internal tobacco documents and admitted that nicotine is addictive.
Thursday's settlement was substantially based on the same terms as the March agreement, Brooke said.

"We now have class action settlements in both federal and state court, which, upon approval, will give Brooke and Liggett near-universal protection," said Bennett LeBow, chief executive of Brooke Group.
The settlement agreement calls for Liggett to stop marketing its cigarettes to children and adolescents and to add strong warnings on cigarette packs regarding the addictive nature of nicotine.
Ligget is also obligated to assist in lawsuits brought against other cigarette companies, including Philip Morris Cos. Inc., by providing internal documents, testimony and witnesses.
